versions.text: Standard: Safety-critical air system components of the air system perform their intended functions in the natural and induced environment for the defined service life. This criterion excludes the engine. The environments assessed in this criterion are listed in TABLE II. TABLE II. Natural and induced environments for safety-critical components. Environment Natural, Induced, or Both Notes Temperature Natural and Induced Includes the ambient temperatures for all intended ground and flight envelope altitudes, thermal loading from subsystems and components of the air system, and cooling considerations. Temperature shock Induced Pressure Natural and Induced Pressures for all intended ground and flight envelope altitudes. Includes considerations for air vehicle cabin pressurization. TABLE II. Natural and induced environments for safety-critical components – Continued. Environment Natural, Induced, or Both Notes Rapid decompression Induced Solar radiation (sunshine) Natural and Induced Includes the combination of natural environment forcing functions, including wind speed, and the physical and chemical characteristics of the materiel itself. Humidity Natural Rain Natural Includes components in areas that would be exposed to water intrusion such as those near open doors. Addresses wind velocity. Icing or Freezing rain Natural Addresses wind velocity. Immersion Induced Contamination by fluids Induced Fungus Natural Induced Sand and dust Natural Includes wind speeds. Salt fog and corrosive environments Natural and Induced Includes gunfire gases, missile gases, sulfur and nitrogen oxides. Acceleration Induced Addresses the steady-state inertia loads induced by platform acceleration, deceleration, and maneuver in the service environment, including crash landing loads (static acceleration test). Obtain acceleration values for testing from the air vehicle structural loads analyses. Vibration Induced Includes mechanical, acoustic, and gunfire vibration and addresses the effect of dynamic pressures. Acquire measured data from the air vehicle for these vibration parameters. Shock Induced Addresses the materiel’s ability to physically and functionally withstand the shocks encountered in handling, transportation, and service environments including crash situations (transient shock test). Tailor the shock values to align with air vehicle representative field measurements of shock. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis. (1) Conduct analysis of post-test data for component qualification testing to identify and assess any failures and design changes (proposed or implemented) to ensure final, tested configuration is understood. (2) Conduct analysis for components qualified by TSO authorization to address differences with air system intended usage, any changes from the original certification, and deviations documented in the TSO authorization to ensure an equivalent level of safety and that the component performs its intended functions. Analysis identifies environment verification, including those altered or impacted by installation or integration (e.g., vibration and temperature), to be addressed through other MoCs of this criterion. Note: a TSO authorization is not an approval to install and use the component in the air system. (3) Analysis for components that are qualified by similarity address differences in installation, integration, and intended usage from the originally qualified component to ensure an equivalent level of safety and no increased risk to operations through use of qualification by similarity. (4) Analysis of available environment verification data for the components confirms operation in all intended natural and induced environments. While the analysis addresses any available environment verification data, the minimum data set addresses twice the intended duration of flight test and the environment to be encountered during flight test. The analysis addresses any gaps between actual test data and environmental requirements and any configuration changes made after completion of verification activities, providing an equivalent level of safety assessment and that the component performs its intended functions. Verification data includes test data, specification sheets, and ICDs that show intended function for all natural and induced environments. Test. (1) Lab test: Conduct component testing IAW the tailored MIL-STD-810 for a subset of the life cycle of the component and in modes representative of flight (e.g., powered-on testing). At a minimum, the testing encompasses twice the intended duration of flight test and the environment to be encountered during flight test. MIL-STD-810 contains tailoring instructions with general guidelines in Part One and specific guidelines in each method of Part Two. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Analysis. (5) Analysis of environment verification data for the components confirms operation in all intended natural and induced environments. The analysis addresses any gaps between actual test data and environmental requirements and any configuration changes made after completion of verification activities, providing an equivalent level of safety assessment and that the component performs its intended functions. Verification data includes test data, specification sheets, and ICDs that show intended function for all natural and induced environments. Test. (2) Lab test: Conduct component testing IAW the tailored MIL-STD-810 for the life cycle of the component, including shipping, transportation, storage, logistics supply, mission use, and sortie use. Conduct testing in modes representative of flight (e.g., powered-on testing). Tailoring instructions are contained within MIL-STD-810 with general guidelines in Part One and specific guidelines in each method of Part Two.
